text:
The unemployment rate is 7.6% and the fed funds rate is about 0.13%, which points to early 2013. Gold fell sharply (-7.7% in one month, -17.8% from its 12-month high), consistent with the April 2013 crash. Unemployment was 7.6% in the March 2013 data, published in April, and it was also 7.6% in April, published in May, before falling to 7.5%.

The 10-year yield at 1.70% suggests April 2013, when it ended around 1.70%. At the end of May it was about 2.13%. Headline CPI of 1.48% fits March 2013 (1.5%), and April was 1.1%. The 3-month average payroll gain of 168k fits March 2013 data (the March payroll gain was weak at 88k).

A one-month gold drop of 7.7% fits April 2013, which was about -7.7%. The 1-month US large-cap return of +2.3% also matches April 2013 (about +1.9%). This is therefore the end of April 2013, with the latest unemployment reading being March's 7.6%.
